intro: Three of the four letter groups follow the same rule, and one doesn't. Turn the letters into their places in the alphabet (A = 1 … Z = 26) and look for the rule.

tips.title: Number the letters
tips.body: Write each letter's place under it: A = 1 … Z = 26 (remember EJOTY: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25). Most rules become number rules.

tips.title: Look at the jumps
tips.body: Find how far each letter is from the next: equal jumps (+2, +2), growing jumps (+1, +2, +3) or backwards (−1, −1).

tips.title: Pairs 13 apart
tips.body: A–N, B–O, C–P … Z–M are opposite each other when the alphabet is written in two rows of 13.

tips.title: Vowels and repeats
tips.body: Check whether the groups start with a vowel, contain one, or repeat a letter. These simple rules come up often.

tips.title: Add or multiply the places
tips.body: Some rules use arithmetic on the places: the first two add up to the third, or the product is a cube or square.
